title: 3D Solids: Cylinders, Cones, Spheres and Cubes
standard_text: K.6B identify three-dimensional solids, including cylinders, cones, spheres, and cubes, in the real world; K.6C identify two-dimensional components of three-dimensional objects; K.6E classify and sort a variety of regular and irregular two- and three-dimensional figures regardless of orientation or size
meta_desc: Free kindergarten 3D solid worksheets for Texas TEKS K.6B, K.6C and K.6E: spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders in the real world, flat faces, and flat or solid. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Solids are not flat: sphere, cube, cone, cylinder.
key_sub: A can is a cylinder with circle faces.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Solids are not flat: sphere, cube, cone, cylinder.
  • A sphere is a ball. A cube has 6 square faces.
  • A cylinder is like a can. A cone is like an ice cream cone.
  • The flat faces of solids are 2D shapes: a can has circle faces.

Examples

Example

A can of soup

2 flat circle faces

Answer: cylinder

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up a circle and a sphereA circle is flat; a sphere is a ball.
Mixing up a square and a cubeA square is one face of a cube.
Thinking a turned cone is something elseTurning does not change the solid.
